verdict: Arm A argues better on evidence and verification: it closes alternate paths with constants and tests, tests the proposed remedy against the code (LB13, LB14, LA8, LB21), and cites the shipped master version as independent confirmation, but it pays in length (median 335 vs 126 words, about 20 vs 11 words per sentence) and twice rejects a claim on a premise the same run refutes elsewhere (LA10 against LA11/LA13, LB10 against LB8), with LB16 waving off the path LB8 established. Arm B is far more readable and every sentence carries a citation, yet its blocks mostly restate the finding hop by hop, dismiss recovery paths as 'not guaranteed' without testing them, and apply opposite rules to the secondary-reviewer mechanism inside one run (MA5 vs MA11, MB11 vs MB19); pair tally: A wins 21 (8 marginal), B wins 5 (1 marginal), 3 ties.
